descriptions: Before the patch, failure of devm_add_action_or_reset() consumed dbg with scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup as a registered reset action and then the error branch explicitly called scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup(dbg) again, allowing the same resources owned by dbg, including dbg->name according to the patch context, to be freed twice. After the patch, the failure path returns NULL immediately and relies only on devm_add_action_or_reset()'s reset action to perform cleanup once.

semantic_payload.label: Functions implicated by removed or fixed code

suggestions: First-draft detector should anchor on a call to devm_add_action_or_reset(dev, cleanup_fn, arg) used as an if-condition or error-check, where the failure branch directly calls cleanup_fn(arg).
The most precise patch-local sink is the deleted explicit call scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup(dbg), not the return NULL or formatting change.

Model devm_add_action_or_reset() as a barrier/reset API that invokes the supplied cleanup callback with the supplied argument on failure; then flag duplicate manual cleanup of the same callback and same argument on that failure path.
Use local AST plus local CFG within the affected function first; no cross-file analysis is needed for the initial checker because the callback and argument identity are visible at the call site.

Treat exact callback identity and exact argument identity as strong first-pass conditions; details of what scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup frees, such as dbg->name, can be a secondary refinement rather than a required initial match.
Do not require a separate free() call in the same function; the vulnerability is duplicated cleanup callback execution, where the actual free may be inside the callback.

patterns: Remove the explicit scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup(dbg) call from the devm_add_action_or_reset() failure branch.
Keep the early return NULL after devm_add_action_or_reset() failure so the setup function stops without a second cleanup invocation.
Rely on devm_add_action_or_reset() to run scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup on failure instead of manually duplicating the cleanup action.

patch_semantic_context.patch_excerpt:
commit 39b13dce1a91cdfc3bec9238f9e89094551bd428
Author: Su Hui <suhui@nfschina.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 11 18:40:02 2024 +0800

    firmware: arm_scmi: Fix the double free in scmi_debugfs_common_setup()
    
    Clang static checker(scan-build) throws below warning：
      |  drivers/firmware/arm_scmi/driver.c:line 2915, column 2
      |        Attempt to free released memory.
    
    When devm_add_action_or_reset() fails, scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup()
    will run twice which causes double free of 'dbg->name'.
    
    Remove the redundant scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup() to fix this problem.
    
    Fixes: c3d4aed763ce ("firmware: arm_scmi: Populate a common SCMI debugfs root")
    Signed-off-by: Su Hui <suhui@nfschina.com>
    Reviewed-by: Cristian Marussi <cristian.marussi@arm.com>
    Message-Id: <20241011104001.1546476-1-suhui@nfschina.com>
    Signed-off-by: Sudeep Holla <sudeep.holla@arm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/firmware/arm_scmi/driver.c b/drivers/firmware/arm_scmi/driver.c
index 88c5c4ff4bb6..a477b5ade38d 100644
--- a/drivers/firmware/arm_scmi/driver.c
+++ b/drivers/firmware/arm_scmi/driver.c
@@ -2976,10 +2976,8 @@ static struct scmi_debug_info *scmi_debugfs_common_setup(struct scmi_info *info)
 	dbg->top_dentry = top_dentry;
 
 	if (devm_add_action_or_reset(info->dev,
-				     scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup, dbg)) {
-		scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup(dbg);
+				     scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup, dbg))
 		return NULL;
-	}
 
 	return dbg;
 }

1. Decide if customization of program state is necessary:
   • No program state maps are required here since we only need to detect a redundant cleanup call by comparing callee names and AST contexts.

2. Choose the callback to hook:
   • Use the checkPreCall callback to intercept any call to scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup.
   • Use the checkBranchCondition callback or AST traversal within checkPreCall to determine if the cleanup call is inside an error handling branch where devm_add_action_or_reset has already been invoked.

3. Implementation steps per callback:

   (a) In checkPreCall:
       • When a call is intercepted, check if its callee’s name is "scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup".
       • Once such a call is identified, use the utility function findSpecificTypeInParents to climb up the AST and locate a parent IfStmt.
       • Retrieve the condition expression of that IfStmt.
       • Use the utility function ExprHasName on the condition expression to verify if it contains the call to devm_add_action_or_reset.
           ▪ This indicates that the branch corresponds to the error path where devm_add_action_or_reset was evaluated.
       • If the above check passes, report a bug with a clear and short message indicating that there is a redundant cleanup call that may cause a double free.

   (b) (Optional) In checkBranchCondition:
       • Alternatively (or in addition) you could use this callback to review the condition of an if statement.
       • Look for the appearance of devm_add_action_or_reset in the condition.
       • Flag the branch as suspicious and possibly annotate its state.
       • Then, in checkPreCall for cleanup calls, consult this flag.
       ▪ This step is optional since the combined check in checkPreCall using the parent AST traversal should be sufficient.

4. Reporting the bug:
   • Generate the error node and a bug report using std::make_unique<BasicBugReport> or std::make_unique<PathSensitiveBugReport>.
   • The report message should be short and clear, e.g., "Redundant cleanup call leads to double free."

------------------------------------------------------------

patch_semantic_context.knighter_pattern_excerpt:
## Bug Pattern

The bug pattern is the redundant cleanup invocation in the error path where an automatic cleanup mechanism is already in place. In this patch, the cleanup function (scmi_debugfs_common_cleanup) is called explicitly after devm_add_action_or_reset() fails, even though devm_add_action_or_reset() already ensures that the cleanup is performed. This redundancy leads to a double free of the resource dbg->name. The underlying issue is mixing manual cleanup calls with device-managed (automatic) cleanup actions, which can result in freeing memory twice.
